newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truck bosses raise bonus offer - union.
newsitem.headline: French truck bosses raise bonus offer - union.

text.p: French road haulage employers doubled their offer of a one-time bonus to striking drivers to 3,000 francs ($600) on Friday in an effort to end a 12-day-old blockade of the nation's roads, a union negotiator said.

"It's up to the strikers on the roadblocks to decide," said Roger Poletti, head of the Force Ouvriere transport workers' union. An employers' representative confirmed the figure but said it was a repackaging of a previous pay offer.

The unions earlier signed five agreements with employers covering early retirement and a range of other subjects but negotiations were continuing at the Transport Ministry on the central issues of pay and working hours.
Government mediator Robert Cros said he had been put in charge of ensuring the accords were implemented and proposing a draft decree on working time by December 15 in consultation with the parties.
Some 225 roadblocks were still in place across France, down from 250 on Thursday, but radio reports said some provincial blockades were being lifted.

Petrol rationing was in force in almost half of the country and more than one-third of the 18,000 filling stations had run out of fuel. The strike has disrupted industry in France and neighbouring countries and cut supplies of fresh produce.
